change.title: pr-33832-flat
change.description: Add AuthzClientCryptoProvider for authorization client cryptographic operations
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: Removing the multiple-provider check lets a FIPS/non-FIPS mix on the classpath pick a provider silently
findings.body: Before this change, `detectProvider` threw `IllegalStateException` when more than one `CryptoProvider` was found. Now it sorts by `order()` and takes the first one. `DefaultCryptoProvider`, `WildFlyElytronProvider` and `FIPS1402Provider` all return 200 (DefaultCryptoProvider.java:83-85, WildFlyElytronProvider.java:76-78, FIPS1402Provider.java:114-116). When two of them are on the classpath, the stable sort keeps ServiceLoader (classpath) order, and the losers are logged only at debug level (lines 64-70). So a deployment that has both `keycloak-crypto-default` and `keycloak-crypto-fips1402` used to fail at startup. Now it can quietly run on the non-FIPS BouncyCastle provider, and nothing at default log levels says so. This affects every caller of `CryptoIntegration.init`: `KeycloakApplication.startup()` (services/.../KeycloakApplication.java:89), the admin CLI (`Globals.java:44`) and the testsuite `CryptoInitRule`. The Quarkus server is not affected because it calls `setProvider` explicitly (KeycloakRecorder.java:214). The new ordering only needs a fallback provider to lose against the real ones. Keep the fail-fast when two or more providers share the top `order()` value, and throw the same message as before.

findings.title: One default-size EC key is used for ES256, ES384 and ES512, so the round trip compares truncated values
findings.body: `KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC").genKeyPair()` makes one key on the JDK's default curve (P-256 on older JDKs, P-384 on newer ones), and all three tests use it. When the key's r/s are longer than `signLength/2` (for example a P-384 key under ES256, where r/s are up to 48 bytes and `len` is 32), `integerToBytes` (AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:153-156) silently keeps only the last `len` bytes. `rsConcat` and `rsConcat2` are then both truncated the same way, so `assertArrayEquals` passes on a signature that cannot be valid. ES512 is never tested with a P-521 key either. The test can't catch a bug in the length handling. Generate a key per algorithm (`initialize(new ECGenParameterSpec("secp256r1"/"secp384r1"/"secp521r1"))`). Also check that `asn1Des` verifies with `Signature.verify` against the public key, or equals the original `sign`, instead of only checking that the round trip is self-consistent.

findings.title: Two encoder calls build objects that are never used
findings.body: Lines 114-115 (`ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger)` and the same for `s`) build encoders and throw them away. The returned sequence builds its own encoders on lines 119-120. Remove both lines.

contracts.action: AuthzClient.create(Configuration) now calls CryptoIntegration.init with the authz client's classloader
contracts.equivalent_path: KeycloakApplication.startup() and admin-cli Globals call CryptoIntegration.init(classLoader) the same way before using crypto
contracts.before_after: Same as the siblings: init runs once (double-checked lock), and later calls are no-ops. If another provider was set first (for example by setProvider), it is kept.
contracts.visible_effect: ECDSAAlgorithm.concatenatedRSToASN1DER/asn1derToConcatenatedRS now resolve a provider instead of throwing 'Please init first'
contracts.failure_mode: If no provider is on the classpath, init throws IllegalStateException out of create(). With the authz client jar, its own service file guarantees at least one provider.

contracts.action: detectProvider picks the highest order() provider instead of failing on several
contracts.equivalent_path: Quarkus KeycloakRecorder.setCryptoProvider picks the provider explicitly from FipsMode
contracts.before_after: Before: more than one provider meant an IllegalStateException. After: AuthzClientCryptoProvider (100) loses to Default/Elytron/FIPS (200), but ties among those three are settled by classpath order.
contracts.visible_effect: The wrong provider is chosen silently; the ignored providers are logged only at debug level
contracts.failure_mode: A FIPS plus default classpath no longer fails fast (reported as a finding)

contracts.action: ECDSAAlgorithm static helpers are served by AuthzClientCryptoProvider's ECDSA implementation
contracts.before_after: DER to R||S conversion uses the minimal-DER BigInteger encoding; r/s are left-padded or truncated to signLength/2
contracts.visible_effect: JWS ES* signatures produced by the client
contracts.failure_mode: Malformed DER gives IOException. A key curve that doesn't match signLength is silently truncated. Every other provider method throws UnsupportedOperationException (for example getSignature, used by AsymmetricSignatureVerifierContext:63).

summary: The PR adds a minimal ECDSA-only crypto provider to the authz client and initialises crypto in `AuthzClient.create`. To make that work, `CryptoIntegration` now orders providers by `order()` and no longer fails when it finds several. The main problem is that the three real providers all return 200. A classpath that mixes FIPS and non-FIPS providers, which used to fail at startup, now silently picks one and logs it only at debug. This affects KeycloakApplication, the admin CLI and the testsuite; Quarkus is not affected because it sets the provider explicitly. The new test uses one default-size EC key for all three algorithms, so for at least two of them it checks a round trip on truncated r/s values and never verifies a signature. There is also a small cleanup: two unused encoder calls.
